A website for a local business is not always about pages.

Often, it is about where pricing lives, who updates the legal details, how service pages are assembled, what Google sees, what AI assistants understand, and whether the Client can leave without losing control.

I broke down a model where the website is built as managed infrastructure: Astro, TypeScript, Cloudflare, declarative content, JSON-LD, llms.txt, quality gates, and a change lifecycle.

Not as a fashionable stack. As a way to remove chaos from operations. 🧩

The most uncomfortable question: does the business really need the freedom to "move blocks around" - or does it need a system i.e. hard to break with an accidental edit?
